example_raw: Dare we run the risk of even one child or adult turning to violent crime because they think it is ok? (Greece; 2010; English)

positives: Dare we ask for more time?
Dare anyone challenge the new rules?
negatives: I dare you to jump over that fence.
How dare you speak to me like that!

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form 'didn\'t dare' + infinitive without 'to' to talk about not being brave enough to do something.
example_raw:
She didn't dare think about him and the possibility that he would never come back. (Sweden; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Swedish; Pass)

Since we didn't dare move our feet, we were slowly swaying to the left and to the right, backwards and forwards. (Turkey; C2 MASTERY; 2001; Turkish; Pass)

positives: She didn't dare look back at the explosion.
They didn't dare say a word during the meeting.
negatives: I didn't dare to dream about winning.
He didn't dare me to do it.

can_do_statement: Can use 'how dare … !' to express disapproval or offense about something
example_raw:
How dare people say that we don't practice sport! (Spain; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1999; Catalan; Pass)

… how dare you say that this event was a complete failure! (France; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2000; French; Pass)

positives: How dare they cancel the show!
How dare you come into my house!
negatives: Dare you tell her the truth?
I dare say she is right.

can_do_statement: Can use 'will' + 'be able to' + infinitive to talk about possibility and ability.
example_raw:
Will you be able to come this time? (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Portuguese; Pass)

[talking about contact lenses] Without them I will not be able to play football. (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Spanish - European; Pass)

If you need a musical instrument, I can bring my guitar but unfortunately I won't be able to play it because I have never learned it. (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; French; Pass)

positives: I won't be able to finish this tonight.
Will you be able to help me tomorrow?
negatives: I am able to swim very well.
She will be there soon.

can_do_statement: Can use a range of modal verbs + 'be able to' + infinitive.
example_raw:
After finishing school, you might be able to hang out with your friends. (Mexico; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

If we could meet in Switzerland, we should be able to finish the project on the 20th June. (Switzerland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Swiss German; Fail)

I'd be able to take walks without even worrying about inhaling polluted air. (Malaysia; B1 THRESHOLD; 2010; Chinese; Pass)

positives: We might be able to fix the car ourselves.
You should be able to see the mountain from here.
negatives: I will be able to do it later.
He is able to run fast.

can_do_statement: Can use 'be allowed to' to talk about permission.
example_raw:
My mother went with me on this trip because I wasn't allowed to go by myself. (Uruguay; B1 THRESHOLD; 2002; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

You won't be allowed to do what you want and you won't enjoy yourself. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Authorization and permission granted by external authority

positives: She isn't allowed to stay out late.
We were allowed to enter the building.
negatives: I allowed him to go.
They are allowing us to stay.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of expressions with 'be' + infinitive ('be allowed to', 'be supposed to', 'be able to') with present and past forms of 'be' and with modal 'will'.
example_raw:
First of all, if you are allowed to go out of the building in your break, you should do it. (Cyprus; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Greek; Pass)

Perhaps you will be allowed to go on holiday with your friends next year. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; German; Pass)

The film is supposed to start at 7.00 pm so we'd better meet at 6.30 pm. See you there! (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Portuguese; Pass)

I was supposed to be meeting my friend Laura but she didn't come. (France; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; French; Pass)

I am sorry but I  am not able to meet you next Tuesday. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; German; Pass)

We were able to choose the songs ourselves and so I liked them very much. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; German; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Core modality using 'be' for capability, expectation, and permission

positives: I am supposed to finish my homework.
They are not able to see the stage.
negatives: They supposed it was true.
She allowed the dog inside.

can_do_statement: Can use 'was supposed to', 'were supposed to' to refer to past or future arrangements which may not have happened or may change.
example_raw:
I am really sorry, but I will have to make some changes to my trip. I was supposed to arrive on 11th June 2003, but I will arrive the next month. (Mexico; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

It was supposed to be on Tuesday at 1.00pm. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Portuguese; Pass)

We were supposed to meet at noon with some friends, but they called her to ask if we could meet at the restaurant. (Mexico; B1 THRESHOLD; 2005; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

positives: We were supposed to go yesterday.
I was supposed to tell you about the change.
negatives: I am supposed to go tomorrow.
They supposed it was a joke.

can_do_statement: Can use the full range of expressions with 'be' + infinitive ('be likely to', 'be due to', 'be meant to', 'be bound to', 'be sure to', 'be certain to', 'be obliged to') with present and past forms of 'be' and with modal 'will' .
example_raw:
People who read books are likely to be more knowledgeable. (Argentina; B2 VANTAGE; 2008; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

I'm bound to feel nervous. (France; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; French; Pass)

According to our new marketing strategy, we are sure to increase our turnover and our profit. (Austria; B2 VANTAGE; 2008; German; Pass)

[talking about a new job] I am due to start on Monday 4 June. (Georgia (Republic of); B2 VANTAGE; 2007; Georgian; Fail)

I would like to inform you that as of 1st of June all operational staff will be obliged to use identity cards. (Poland; B2 VANTAGE; 2006; Polish; Pass)

Sleepy and unwilling to take part of the conference, I was obliged to spend the evening listening to the soft voice of a man who was famous for his boring performances. (Italy; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Italian; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Degrees of certainty, expectation, and obligation

positives: We are bound to make mistakes.
She is certain to win the competition.
negatives: I am supposed to leave now.
He was able to finish the puzzle.

can_do_statement: Can use 'was able to', 'were able to' to talk about facts in the past.
example_raw:
[about a bus journey] She was able to get a good seat and she unexpectedly got to school early. (Philippines; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Tagalog; Pass)

… sales had increased recently because of the good performance of our staff so we were able to improve the quality of our products ... (Ecuador; B1 THRESHOLD; 2010; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Past capability leading to a factual outcome

positives: I was able to find my lost keys.
They weren't able to complete the test.
negatives: I am able to speak three languages.
She will be able to join us later.

can_do_statement: Can use 'be meant to' to talk about ideal states.
example_raw:
Animals are meant to be free, and man should be very careful about interfering with nature. (Swedish, B2 VANTAGE, Pass, 1993)

Primary school is meant to be there so that you build all the basics of your education. (French, B2 VANTAGE, ===NONE===, 2011)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Expressing how things should naturally be

positives: We are meant to learn from our mistakes.
It is meant to be a relaxing vacation.
negatives: I meant to call you earlier.
She was bound to find out the truth.

can_do_statement: Can use 'be due to' and, more formally, 'be to' to talk about things that are scheduled or expected.
example_raw:
I have attached the … company law directive enacted 2 years ago and which is due to be implemented by 2008. (Austria; B2 VANTAGE; 2007; German; Pass)

The programme was due to start at midday. (Argentina; B2 VANTAGE; 1997; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

I am sorry that I cannot attend the meeting at head office as expected, as I am to go on a business trip to New York then. (China; B2 VANTAGE; 2002; Chinese; Pass)

I was to take exams in two weeks and had to study hard. (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Greek; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Future plans based on fixed schedules

positives: The train is due to arrive at noon.
I am to start my new job on Monday.
negatives: I am going to the store.
It is due to the bad weather.

can_do_statement: Can use 'be' (+modifier) 'likely to' to talk about probability.
example_raw:
And whenever money is involved, some problems are likely to happen. (Spain; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; Spanish - European; Pass)

I am very likely to make mistakes which I would like to avoid. (Poland; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Polish; Pass)

positives: It is very likely to rain this evening.
They are likely to forget the appointment.
negatives: I like to play basketball.
She is more likely to succeed.

can_do_statement: Can use '(much) more/less' to modify 'likely' in a comparison.
example_raw:
In case of an accident, one is more likely to be badly injured when riding a bicycle. (Poland; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Polish; Pass)

Since they are more and better educated when they leave school at 18 years old, their minds are more mature and they are more sensible. They are more likely to have better jobs and a better life, and much less likely to cause problems to other people. (B2 VANTAGE; 2009; Chinese; Pass)

positives: You are much less likely to get sick if you wash your hands.
Older cars are more likely to break down.
negatives: She is likely to arrive on time.
I liked the movie more than the book.

can_do_statement: Can use 'be supposed to' to talk about hearsay or supposition.
example_raw:
That woman is supposed to have killed her husbands (at least two), because she wanted their money. (Spain; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; Spanish - European; Pass)

The lake is supposed to be very beautiful. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1998; Swedish; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Information received through rumor or popular belief

positives: The new restaurant is supposed to be amazing.
He is supposed to have won the lottery.
negatives: I am supposed to finish my homework.
They supposed that he was right.
